summary: SpatialWorkingSetIndex retained the validated source F# list, so query paid list traversal twice: indexing entries[index] for each selected ordinal walked the list by ordinal, and reporting TotalEntryCount via entries.Length walked the whole list even when the selection was the first entry. Retaining the entries once in private array storage at create (Rendering#1470, merge bd10d241, Delivery #1469) removed both without changing the public API, ordering, counters, refusal order or bucket construction. CLR before/after on one shared 3-CPU dev host with identical selections and counters: at 300,000 entries median per query was 100 late visible 25,637 to 45.9 us, one late visible 546.6 to 33.6 us, first ordinal 291.8 to 31.6 us; no cell regressed beyond noise, create allocation about +0.2%, candidate create time lower at 100,000 and 300,000 entries for an unexplained reason that is not claimed as an improvement. Lesson: a first-ordinal control isolates the length traversal, so a late-versus-early comparison alone under-detects it; compare against a different-source-length reference too. Limits: the real M9 browser fixture places visible entries first, so its gate (hosted extent cost ratio 0.999) shows the packed consumer unchanged and is not evidence of the late-lookup speedup; no timing threshold, Home B1-B8 verdict, publication or installed adoption is implied. Bucket construction still appends to per-bucket lists quadratically and was deliberately left unchanged.
title: Spatial working-set query cost came from ordinal traversal in selection and in TotalEntryCount
